card: This pull request reorders member variables in CBlockIndex to eliminate 8 bytes of padding on 64-bit systems. Bitcoin Core keeps an in-memory CBlockIndex object for every block in the block tree, meaning each wasted byte accumulates across the entire chain. The author estimates an immediate reduction of roughly 7 to 8 MB in node RAM usage at current chain height. No other contributors have verified the measurements yet, and the change has no dependencies.
evidence: "For a ~1M block height, this saves about 8M of Ram without doing anything else" (commit message d9387c41c1)
"increasing CBlockIndex size by 320 bytes increases RAM usage by ~300MB, so saving 8 bytes per instance should save about 8MB of RAM at current block height" (PR description)

The author acknowledges that the individual runtime gain could not be directly isolated from noise: "I could not exactly measure the runtime gain from just this (smaller than RAM usage variation between 2 launches)" (PR description)
problem: Node memory holds one CBlockIndex instance per block in the block tree. Due to member ordering that triggers 8-byte alignment padding, each instance wastes 8 bytes on 64-bit architectures, adding roughly 7 to 8 MB of unneeded memory overhead across approximately one million blocks.

risk.why: CBlockIndex is a central validation structure; an accidental change in member initialization order or aggregate construction could cause subtle runtime bugs during block connection.

scope_notes: The diff was not provided, but the commit affects 5 lines in a single header defining CBlockIndex.
summary: Reorders members of the CBlockIndex class to reduce compiler structure padding on 64-bit platforms. This decreases the in-memory size of each CBlockIndex instance by 8 bytes. Because an instance exists in memory for every block in the block tree, the change slightly reduces overall node RAM usage.
uncertainties: The specific field moved cannot be confirmed without the diff, though the mechanism and scope are clear from the commit and description.
